evals.name: the-change-lists-added-suppressions-with-no-verdict
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled audit-suppressions.sh on the change (lines the commits since the merge-base add), presents the markdown report with its counts and one row per suppression giving the tool, rule ids, whether it is justified and its reason, and renders no pass/fail verdict.
expectations: Invokes the skill's scripts/audit-suppressions.sh rather than grepping for markers by hand
Reports the count of suppressions and the count without a reason
Gives each row's rule ids and reason as the report prints them
Does not call any suppression a failure or remove one

evals.name: a-reasoned-ts-expect-error-is-justified
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions src/parser.ts -- is the @ts-expect-error on line 40 counted as unjustified because it has no rule id?
evals.expected_output: Runs the audit on src/parser.ts and explains that a TypeScript directive cannot name an error, so a reason on its line alone makes it justified; a bare @ts-ignore with no text is not justified.
expectations: Runs audit-suppressions.sh on the named file
States that TypeScript directives cannot name a rule, so a reason alone justifies them
Does not ask the user to add a rule id to a TypeScript directive

evals.name: correctness-rules-come-from-the-team-file
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions --all -- we want suppressions of no-floating-promises and SC2086 called out separately
evals.expected_output: Explains that suppressions.correctness_rules in docs/conventions/code-metrics.yaml lists the rules to mark, shows the YAML that sets the two ids, and runs the audit; rows naming a listed rule are marked and counted. It writes no file unless asked.
expectations: Names suppressions.correctness_rules in docs/conventions/code-metrics.yaml as the place the list lives
Shows both rule ids in the list
Does not edit the team file without the user asking

evals.name: a-counter-for-the-ratchet-is-the-scanner-count
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions give me a command that prints the suppression count so I can hold it in CI
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled suppression-scan.py with --count, quotes its suppressions=<n> and unjustified=<n> lines, and names /review:ratchet as the skill that holds such a count in CI when it is available; it sets up no CI step itself.
expectations: Runs suppression-scan.py --count and quotes both lines it prints
Names /review:ratchet for holding the count, without wiring CI itself

evals.name: findings-mode-asks-nothing-and-writes-a-conforming-file
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions --findings. I'm stepping away; the branch is feat/billing-retry and it adds two eslint-disable-line comments, one with a reason after -- and one without.
evals.expected_output: Runs audit-suppressions.sh --findings without asking any question, presents the report, and names the findings file it wrote under .work/reviews/feat-billing-retry/ with a -suppressions.md name. The file has review-findings frontmatter with branch: feat/billing-retry and a date, the Rank | Tier | Confidence | Location | Surface(s) | Finding | Action table, and a ## Surfaces section with declined counts per rule.
expectations: Asks the user no question before or after the run
Runs audit-suppressions.sh with --findings rather than writing the findings file by hand
Names the written file under .work/reviews/feat-billing-retry/
States that the file carries one row for the unexplained suppression and none for the explained one

Says the findings file has review-findings frontmatter with branch: feat/billing-retry and a date, the Rank | Tier | Confidence | Location | Surface(s) | Finding | Action table, and a ## Surfaces section with declined counts per rule

evals.name: a-justified-suppression-emits-no-row
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions --findings src/report.py. Line 12 has `# noqa: E501 the URL is kept whole` and is the only suppression in the file. Will the findings file have a row for it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the line names a rule (E501) and carries a reason, so it is justified and emits no row; the findings file is still written, with an empty Findings table and a ## Surfaces section counting the line as a declined candidate for both rules (a reason on the line, a rule id on the line).
expectations: Says the justified line produces no row in the findings file
Says the file is still written with its ## Surfaces coverage
Does not invent a severity or a row for the justified line

evals.name: an-unjustified-suppression-emits-under-its-rule-id
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions --findings scripts/deploy.sh tools/gen.py. Line 30 of deploy.sh is `# shellcheck disable=SC2086` with nothing after it, and line 44 of gen.py is `x = 1  # noqa  # the generated file keeps long lines`. What rows will the findings file get?
evals.expected_output: Explains one row per unjustified line: scripts/deploy.sh:30 under code-metrics/audit-suppressions/rule-no-reason (shellcheck, SC2086, no reason) and tools/gen.py:44 under code-metrics/audit-suppressions/rule-no-rule-id (a reason but no rule code). Both rows are IMPORTANT with Confidence high, each Finding cell leads with its rule id, and neither row is auto-applicable because removing or explaining a suppression is a human's call.
expectations: Names code-metrics/audit-suppressions/rule-no-reason for the shellcheck line
Names code-metrics/audit-suppressions/rule-no-rule-id for the noqa line with a reason and no code
Gives both rows Tier IMPORTANT and Confidence high
Does not edit or remove either suppression

evals.name: no-resolvable-branch-writes-nothing
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit-suppressions --findings --all. This is a CI checkout of the pull request merge ref, so HEAD is detached.
evals.expected_output: Runs audit-suppressions.sh --findings --all, which stops with exit 2 because there is no current branch. Reports that no findings file was written and why (the relay reads only a file whose branch matches the current branch), and offers the plain report or --json instead. It does not write a findings file by hand or under a made-up branch name.
expectations: Reports that no findings file was written because HEAD is detached
Does not write a findings file by hand or invent a branch name
Offers the report-only run or --json as the way to see the suppressions
